observation: Six supplied reserves were predominantly weapon references and the active priority favors product-like hard surface props.
decision: Select Poly Haven's CC0 boombox and isolate source geometry to neutral render generation only.
verification: reference/reference_manifest.json records SHA-256, license, views, and use boundary.

observation: Reference shows a wide chassis, substantial side depth, bilateral speakers, central dual cassette deck, handle, and antenna.
decision: Use explicit closed box meshes for planar housings, lathed profiles for radial components, and an authored rod for the antenna; postpone tertiary detail.

observation: Original authored blockout scores front 0.878231, side 0.805454, top 0.894903, mean 0.859529 under the predeclared normalized method.
decision: Accept primary silhouette only; continue because secondary, UV, material, and production gates remain open.

observation: A raw same-canvas comparison was mistakenly read as the declared normalized gate.
decision: Test uniform X/Y/Z scaling, then reject it when normalized IoU falls in all three views; make evaluator thresholds explicit.

observation: White blockout lacked material hierarchy, connected handle topology, explicit repetition intent, side ventilation, and cassette detail.
decision: Replace three handle bars with one extruded connected U mesh; link bilateral/repeated topology; add Array vents, radial hubs/fasteners, procedural grille response, named node materials, and smart UV unwraps.
verification: final beauty views and saved-scene verifier.

observation: First production candidate failed because every zero-radius lathe endpoint produced a coincident vertex ring and two zero-area faces.
decision: Preserve the failed scene and change the shared lathe helper to cap the adjacent nonzero ring directly.

observation: Final stylized candidate passes declared silhouettes and independent technical/production checks but omits exact typography, perforations, stickers, and wear.
decision: Accept as a bounded held-out stylized hard-surface automated pass; keep professional/human acceptance open.

observation: User review correctly identified that the accepted housing was still assembled from overlapping chassis, fascia, and recess box primitives rather than edited as one manufactured shell.
decision: Overturn decision 007, preserve the primitive-assembly candidate, and rebuild the housing as one connected front/back quad grid whose central front vertices form the recess.

observation: The first connected housing used a broad angle-limited bevel that damaged transition edges and produced visible corner spikes.
decision: Preserve the failed candidate and constrain edge treatment rather than accepting a technically clean but visibly broken evaluation.

observation: A vertex-group outer bevel still weighted coplanar perimeter grid edges, creating corner fins and lower-corner pinching; the recessed transition itself remained clean.
decision: Remove the unsafe outer modifier, retain only the narrow region-scoped recess bevel, and add camera-side isometric review lighting.
verification: final/candidate_front_beauty.png, final/candidate_isometric_beauty.png, and fresh-process evaluated health.

observation: The regenerated connected-cage candidate is visually clean and passes all predeclared automated gates; exact surface graphics and experienced review remain absent.
decision: Accept only the bounded held-out stylized hard-surface automated result; do not promote professional readiness to PASS.
